 Romualdez’s co-accused surrenders, gets conditional immunity
 Daniza Fernandez ,
 ABS-CBN News
 Published November 20, 2026 01:52 PM PHT 
  | 
 Updated November 20, 2026 02:56 PM PHT 
 Former House Speaker and Leyte First District Rep. Martin Romualdez pleads not guilty during his arraignment via videoconference from the Quezon City Jail in Payatas on Sept.16, 2026.  Aaron Favila, AP Photos/Pool  MANILA — The Office of the Ombudsman has granted a co-accused of Leyte Rep. Martin Romualdez “conditional” immunity after he surrendered to authorities.
 Samchan Foreign Exchange Corporation President Felicito Guevarra is facing a plunder charge before the Sandiganbayan Third Division over his alleged involvement in Romualdez and ex-congressman Zaldy Co’s supposed P7.4-billion kickback scheme from government projects.
 AMLC witness: Romualdez's bank transactions hit P4.5 billion during speakership  In a statement on Friday, the Ombudsman said Guevarra surrendered to the National Bureau of Investigation on Nov. 19 after the prosecution pushed for his passport cancellation.
 The anti-graft body granted Guevarra “conditional” immunity as his “testimony and records are necessary to establish the truth” in the case, adding that these “will help the prosecution trace the movement of funds alleged in the charge sheet.”
 ADVERTISEMENT
 Under the “conditional” immunity, Guevarra must cooperate “fully and truthfully,” turn over all of Samchan’s records and devices, remain in the country, and stay under the Department of Justice’s protection.
 “If he breaks any condition, his immunity will be revoked and his prosecution will resume,” the Ombudsman said.
 Samchan has returned all its earnings from flagged transactions to the Bureau of the Treasury.
 “ Restitution  does not erase criminal liability. It is also not the basis of the immunity,” the anti-graft body said.
 P611M recovered from restitution process in flood control fiasco — acting DOJ chief The Ombudsman earlier said Samchan "knowingly participated in, facilitated, or otherwise aided" the supposed laundering of proceeds from unlawful acts.
